turns.doctor_question: Hello, I’m Dr. __. What brings you in today?
turns.patient_response:
Well, I'm here because... look, everybody keeps acting like I’m imagining it. But I know my wife’s relative came into this house to get at me. I mean, my tools don’t move themselves. I work assembly, right? Fabricating parts. You learn real quick that everything has to be exactly where you left it or the whole line stops. I had this foreman once, years ago, who would throw an absolute fit if a socket wrench was even half an inch out of place on the board. He ended up retiring and moving to Ohio, I think... or maybe Indiana. Somewhere with a lot of corn. 

Anyway, my fishing plans don't get spoiled by accident every single weekend either. I used to love going down to the lake, just getting away from the noise, setting up a couple of lines. Catching bass is all about patience. But now? Every time I try to go, something's messed with. After all these months of this going on, I can see plain as day he’s been trying to take over my place and push me out. It's just like how they try to push the older guys out at the shop, you know? Bringing in these young kids right out of high school who can't even read a basic schematic...

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient expresses a fixed, persecutory belief that his wife's relative is secretly entering his home to sabotage his belongings and push him out, despite others telling him he is imagining it.
symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient exhibits tangential speech, drifting off-topic from his main complaint to talk about a former foreman moving to Ohio and young workers at his shop.

turns.doctor_question: How long have you been having these beliefs that someone is trying to get at you and take over your place?
turns.patient_response:
It’s been... I'd say about nine months. Yeah, nine months, ever since my wife’s relative moved into our home. We had to clear out the spare room for him, which meant I had to move my grandfather's old cedar chest out of there by myself. 

That chest is heavy, solid wood, not like that cheap particle board junk everybody buys today. My daughter bought a bookshelf from one of those big box stores last year, and it came with a little bag of wooden pegs and a tiny hex wrench. Took me three hours to put it together, and the thing still wobbled. I told her, you put three heavy textbooks on this, it's gonna fold like a cheap tent. You just can't find good craftsmanship anymore, you know? Nobody takes pride in their work. It's all about mass production and cutting corners. 

But, uh... what were we talking about? Oh, right. Yeah, nine months he's been living under my roof, trying to push me out.

turns.doctor_question: Have you been hearing or seeing things that other people don’t seem to notice?
turns.patient_response: No, I don't... I don't see things that aren't there, if that's what you mean. I'm not crazy. I just see what's right in front of me. Like the tools. You know, speaking of seeing things, the lighting in my garage is terrible. I've been meaning to change out those old fluorescent tubes for years. They hum, you know? That low, constant buzzing sound. It drives you nuts if you're out there trying to concentrate on a project. I was reading this article in a magazine at the dentist's office—Dr. Henderson, good guy, though his receptionist is always chewing gum like a cow with cud—anyway, the article said that fluorescent lights can actually cause headaches because of the flicker rate. It's something to do with the hertz or the cycles per second. I tried explaining that to my wife when I wanted to buy those new LED shop lights, but she said they were too expensive. Everything's too expensive these days, though. Have you seen the price of a decent steak at the grocery store? It's highway robbery. You used to be able to get a nice ribeye for... well, anyway, no, I don't hear voices or see ghosts or anything. Just the reality of what he's doing to me.

turns.doctor_question: During the past nine months, have you felt depressed most days?
turns.patient_response:
Depressed? No, I wouldn't say I'm depressed. Frustrated, sure, but I still get up and go to work every day. Though getting to work is a whole other story lately. The traffic on the interstate has been an absolute nightmare. They've been doing this construction near the overpass for what feels like three years now. I don't know what the city planners are doing. Probably sitting in some air-conditioned office drinking that expensive coffee that takes ten minutes to make. 

My buddy Mike—he drives a delivery truck for a bakery across town—he says the crews just leave the orange cones out even when nobody is working. Total waste of taxpayer money, if you ask me. It's just like how they repaved Elm Street last summer and then dug it right back up two weeks later to fix a water main. You'd think they could coordinate these things, you know? Have a meeting, talk to each other. It's common sense. But common sense isn't so common anymore. 

But yeah, no, I'm not sitting around crying or feeling depressed most days. Just... just trying to hold onto what's mine.

symptom_reasoning.S024: The patient explicitly denies feeling depressed or crying most days.

turns.doctor_question: Have you been using any alcohol, drugs, or new medications around the time these beliefs started?
turns.patient_response:
No, no, nothing like that. I don't do drugs, and I'm just taking my regular blood pressure pill. I don't drink much either, maybe a beer while I'm watching the game. 

Speaking of the game, did you see the playoffs last weekend? Unbelievable. The officiating in this league has just gone completely down the tubes. I mean, that holding call in the fourth quarter? My grandmother could have seen that the defensive end initiated the contact, and she's been legally blind since 2018. It's like these referees are watching a completely different game. I was telling the guys on the assembly line on Monday—we were working on a batch of those new aluminum brackets, the ones with the reinforced flanges—and I said to them, I said, "If I did my job as poorly as these refs do theirs, they'd fire me before lunch." Because on the line, precision matters, right? You get a tolerance off by two millimeters, and the whole assembly won't fit into the housing. We have quality control breathing down our necks every shift. But these referees? They blow a call that costs a team the season, and they just get to go home and collect their paycheck. No accountability. 

But, uh, no. No new medications or drugs or anything. Just my normal routine.

symptom_reasoning.S015: The patient talks excessively, going on a long, unprompted tangent about a football game, referees, and his job on an assembly line before finally returning to the doctor's question.

turns.doctor_question: What exactly do you think your wife’s relative is doing to you?
turns.patient_response:
Look, I’m only here talking to you because everybody keeps acting like I’m imagining it. But I know for a fact my wife’s relative came into this house specifically to get at me. I mean, my tools don’t just get up and move themselves across the workbench. And my fishing plans? Spoiled, every single weekend, and it's not by accident. 

You know, speaking of fishing, the water levels out at the reservoir have been completely messed up this year. The county, or whoever runs the dam, they’ve been letting out way too much water. You go out there to launch the boat, and the ramp is just caked in this thick, foul-smelling mud. I spent three hours last month just trying to pressure wash the hull of my bass boat because of that muck. And my power washer, it’s one of those gas-powered Hondas—great engine, usually starts on the first pull, but the carburetor gets gummed up if you don't use that fuel stabilizer. You gotta use the blue liquid, not the red stuff. The red stuff actually eats away at the rubber gaskets over time. I tried telling my neighbor that when he borrowed my edger, but did he listen? Of course not. Brought it back sputtering like a dying tractor. People just don't respect other people's property anymore. You buy something nice, you take care of it, and someone else just comes along and ruins it. 

But... yeah, no, it's not an accident what's happening to me. After all these months of this going on, I can see it plain as day. He’s been trying to take over my place and push me out. Just push me right out of my own life.

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient expresses a fixed, persecutory belief that his wife's relative is intentionally moving his tools, spoiling his plans, and trying to push him out of his life.
symptom_reasoning.S021: The patient exhibits tangential speech and derailment, wandering off-topic into a long, loosely associated monologue about reservoir water levels, pressure washers, fuel stabilizers, and his neighbor before returning to the main subject.

turns.doctor_question: Have you ever had a period of several days or longer when your mood was unusually elevated, irritable, or full of energy?
turns.patient_response:
Elevated? Like, full of energy? No, I wouldn't say that. I mean, I'm just a regular guy. I get tired after a long shift just like anybody else. Though, I'll tell you, the energy drinks these kids are chugging on the floor nowadays, it's a wonder their hearts don't just explode right out of their chests. 

We got this new kid, started about three weeks ago—Tyler, I think his name is. Nice enough kid, but he comes in every morning with one of those massive, brightly colored cans. Looks like battery acid. And he just pounds it before the 7:00 AM whistle. Then he's practically vibrating while he's trying to calibrate the spot welder. I told him, I said, "Tyler, you keep drinking that garbage, you're gonna burn out your adrenal glands." Because I read this article in Popular Mechanics while I was getting my tires rotated—which, by the way, the guy at the shop tried to tell me I needed new brake pads, but I checked them myself last month and there's at least a quarter inch of pad left. They always try to upsell you on the brakes. You go in for a simple rotation and balance, and suddenly you're looking at a $600 bill. It's a racket, the whole auto repair industry. You really gotta know how to do your own maintenance or they'll take you to the cleaners. 

But yeah, no, I don't get all hyped up or anything. I just try to get my rest, even though it's hard to sleep when you know someone's going through your stuff.

turns.doctor_question: Have these beliefs been going on continuously for at least six months?
turns.patient_response:
Yeah, it's been... what, about nine months now? Ever since he moved into the house. Nine long months of this nonsense. 

Speaking of moving in, you wouldn't believe the amount of junk people accumulate. When he brought his boxes over, I had to clear out half the garage just to make room. And my garage, that's my sanctuary, you know? I had my pegboard organized perfectly. Every wrench, every socket, outlined in permanent marker so you know exactly where it goes. It took me three weekends to get it set up like that after we bought the place. We bought the house back in '14, right when the market was starting to recover, but before the prices went completely insane. The inspector tried to tell us the roof only had five years left on it, but I climbed up there myself. Architectural shingles. They were in great shape, just needed a little moss killer on the north-facing side. You spray that zinc sulfate stuff on there, let the rain wash it down, and it kills the moss right down to the roots. If you don't, the roots get under the shingles and lift them up, and then you've got water in your attic. And water damage? That's a nightmare. My brother-in-law had a pipe burst under his sink while they were in Florida for a week. Completely ruined his hardwood floors. They had to rip everything out down to the subfloor. Insurance fought him tooth and nail on it, too. They always try to claim it's "gradual wear and tear" so they don't have to pay out. 

But yeah, nine months. Nine months of him being there, messing with my things, trying to push me out.

turns.patient_response:
Depressed? Elevated? No, no, I haven't had anything like that. I just... I'm just trying to keep my head above water with all this going on, you know? It's stressful, sure, but I'm not, like, depressed or bouncing off the walls. I just want my house back to the way it was. 

Speaking of the house, I was actually looking at the foundation the other day. You know, you really have to keep an eye on the grading around the perimeter. If the soil settles and slopes toward the foundation, you're just asking for a flooded basement. I spent a whole weekend last spring hauling in topsoil, wheelbarrow after wheelbarrow, just to build up the grade around the back patio. The guy at the garden center tried to sell me on this premium compost mix, but I told him, "Look, buddy, I just need fill dirt. I'm not trying to grow prize-winning tomatoes against my siding." Tomatoes are a whole other headache, anyway. You try to grow them here, and if the blight doesn't get them, the hornworms will. Those things are massive, like the size of your thumb, and they can strip a plant bare in a single night. My grandfather used to go out with a flashlight and pick them off by hand. He had this old coffee can filled with soapy water that he'd drop them into. He was a tough old bird, my grandfather. Worked in the steel mills for forty years. Never complained once. Not like people today, you know? 

But, uh, what were you asking? Oh, right, depressed or elevated. No, nothing like that. Just stressed out because of him.

turns.doctor_question: Have you ever heard voices when no one else was around?
turns.patient_response:
Voices? No, no, I don't hear anything like that. My hearing's not exactly what it used to be anyway, to be honest. Thirty years on the assembly floor will do that to you. The stamping presses alone are enough to rattle your teeth right out of your skull. 

OSHA came through a few years back and made management issue everyone these heavy-duty earmuffs. The bright yellow ones. Before that, we just used those little foam plugs, you know? You roll them up between your fingers and stick them in, but half the guys didn't even do it right. They'd just shove them in so they were sticking halfway out of their ears, not doing a lick of good. You gotta let them expand to create a seal. But those new earmuffs they make us wear now, they get so incredibly sweaty in the summer. The shop floor doesn't have AC, just these massive industrial fans that basically just blow hot, dusty air around. It gets up to 95 degrees in there by August. Guys are drinking Gatorade by the gallon just to keep from passing out. I prefer water myself, maybe with a little pinch of salt in it if it's really sweltering. Gatorade's got way too much sugar. It spikes your blood sugar and then you crash right around two o'clock, right when you need to be paying attention so you don't lose a finger in the brake press. 

But anyway, no, I don't hear any voices. Just a little ringing in my ears sometimes from the machines, but that's it.

symptom_reasoning.S020: The patient explicitly denies hearing voices, stating they do not hear anything like that.

turns.doctor_question: Have you ever had any time when your work and daily life were still affected by these beliefs even though you were not feeling depressed or unusually energized?
turns.patient_response:
Well, yeah, of course. I mean, I still get up every morning, pack my lunch, and go down to the plant. I do my assembler work just like I have for the last thirty years. I keep the bills paid, I take care of myself, I mow the lawn... well, when the mower's working, anyway. 

I actually had to rebuild the carburetor on my John Deere last weekend. It's a riding mower, an older model, maybe from the late nineties? Solid steel deck, not like the cheap plastic stuff they sell at the big box stores now. But ethanol gas just destroys those older carburetors. It eats right through the rubber gaskets and clogs up the jets with this sticky varnish. I tell all the guys at work, if you're going to run small engines, you gotta find a station that sells non-ethanol gas. There's a place out on Route 9, an old independent station, that still sells it. Costs about fifty cents more a gallon, but it saves you hours of headaches. You take that carburetor apart, you gotta soak it in carb cleaner, blow out all the tiny little holes with compressed air... and you better make sure you don't lose that little needle valve. It's about the size of a grain of rice, and if you drop it on the garage floor, forget it. You're sweeping for an hour trying to find it. 

But yeah, my daily life is fine. I'm not depressed or energized or whatever. The only trouble is all centered on what's happening in my house with him and my things. That's the real problem.
